title: feed.json, schema version 1
description: The ranked feed snapshot that the publish stage writes for the reader client (ADR-0006). The publisher must produce exactly this shape: unknown fields are rejected here so the contract can't drift silently. Clients must ignore fields they don't know, so additive changes don't break them.

schema_version.description: Major version of this format. It changes only for a breaking change (ADR-0006, 'Versioning'). A client that doesn't support the value keeps its last good feed.

generated_at.description: When the publish stage built this feed. The time window is measured back from here.

run_id.description: Id of the pipeline run that built the feed (RunStats.run_id), e.g. '20261017T173514-077243'. The timestamped copy is stored as feeds/<run_id>.json.

items.description: At most 200 articles, highest score first.

id.description: Article.id: the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the canonical URL. Stable across runs, so the client can key read state and offline copies on it.

title.description: Article.title (the feed's title, falling back to the extracted one).

url.description: Article.canonical_url: the link to the original page.

domain.description: Host of the canonical URL without a leading 'www.', e.g. 'theguardian.com'. Shown as the publisher until sources have display names.

published_at.description: Article.published_at, or null when the publisher gave no usable date.

summary.description: Article.summary: plain text from the feed (no HTML), or null.

lead_image.description: Article.lead_image: absolute URL of the publisher's image, or null.

score.description: Article.score from the rank stage. Items are sorted by it, highest first.

score_breakdown.description: Article.score_breakdown: named score components, e.g. 'topic:<name>', 'source', 'recency'. For explanation only; the client must not recompute the score from it. Never contains 'muted' (muted articles are left out).

extraction_status.description: Article.extraction.status. Clients may show it as a label (e.g. 'Subscriber only' for paywalled) and must tolerate values they don't know.

display.description: How the client shows the item. 'article': open the cleaned content in the reader. 'link': show headline, summary and image, and open the original URL. Decided by the publish stage (ADR-0006, 'Display rule').

word_count.description: Words in the cleaned content, for a reading-time estimate. Null for 'link' items.

content_path.description: For 'article' items, the path of the cleaned article HTML (a sanitised UTF-8 fragment) relative to feed.json in the same store. Null for 'link' items.
